answer.answer:
The court is a rectangle marked out with lines 40 mm wide (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 1.1).
A shuttle landing on a line is 'in': all the lines form part of the area which they define (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 1.3), and it is a fault only if the shuttle lands outside the boundaries of the court, i.e. not on or within the boundary lines (Clause 13.3.1). The line judge indicates whether the shuttle landed 'in' or 'out' on the line(s) assigned (Clause 17.4), and if the shuttle lands in, the Line Judge says nothing but points to the line with the right hand while looking towards the Umpire (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.4).
For contrast, if the shuttle lands out, no matter how far, the Line Judge calls "Out" promptly in a clear voice and signals by extending both arms horizontally (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 8.3) — so a verbal call is made only for 'out', while 'in' is shown by pointing to the line.
